text.p: Investment firm Oppenheimer and Co is closing its Latin America equity research unit, but will retain some operations in the region, a spokesman said on Thursday.
"It's a refocusing of the firm's overall Latin American effort," John Ryan, Oppenheimer's director of corporate communications, said of the moves.
About 20 people will lose their jobs, 18 of them from the firm's Latin American equity research department, Ryan said.

Earlier, Vinod Sehgal, director of Oppenheimer's Latin American research department, said the firm was shutting down Latin America equities, sales trading and research. He said the decision would affect 30 staffers.

But an Oppenheimer inter-office memo obtained by Reuters said the firm plans to concentrate its Latin American operations on direct private equity investment, asset management, fixed income underwriting, sales and trading, as well as some investment banking activities, including mergers and acquisitions.

The changes at the firm are designed to "allow us to better respond to changing market conditions and to continue to grow those businesses which we believe are most closely allied with the firm's core strengths," the memo from Oppenheimer's executive committee said.
